intent_anchor.user_goal: Prove two clients converge through a safe authoritative world-commit boundary.
intent_anchor.current_priority: Verify authority, confirmation and forged-mutation rejection before accepting G6.

claim_under_review: G6-001 requires preview then explicit confirmation before an authoritative commit.
what_i_accept: All 19 server tests and 12 Godot two-client checks pass.
Two clients converge on revision and entity-set hash after the normal pending-preview-confirm-commit flow.
Forged actor, client, owner, direct write, stale revision, invalid schema, altered receipt and replay cases are covered.
Integrated boot, validator, secret scan and executable public-bind scan are clean.
All G6 receipts validate against the canonical MAF step schema and writer paths are disjoint.
what_i_challenge: Both Python and Godot submit_proposal paths accept a client-supplied confirmation.state=confirmed when confirmed_by matches the session actor.
A client can then call commit without ever invoking the explicit confirm_proposal transition, bypassing the required preview-confirm boundary.
strongest_counter_argument: The submitted prompt still declares preview_required=true and the actor matches its session, but a declaration is not evidence that preview was shown or that confirmation occurred as a separate server-observed transition.
missing_evidence: Regression proof that client-supplied confirmed state is rejected before proposal registration and mutation in both runtimes.
Regression proof that commit remains impossible until confirm_proposal succeeds.
The adversarial-review skill references absent schema files, so this object follows its documented fields but could not be validated against that skill schema.
blind_spots: Authentication transport and production multiplayer remain explicitly outside this local POC.
next_action: Apply WO-G6-001-CORRECTION-001 in both authority implementations and rerun all G6 gates plus the confirmation-bypass exploit.
